To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the indentation hardness and indentation modulus of the nanodiamond enhanced with tungsten strengthened aluminum alloys stored in Outer space are lower than the indentation hardness and the indentation modulus of the same material stored under terrestrial conditions.
the indentation modulus of the investigated nanocomposite is slightly higher in the case of the sample stored in Outer space.

the indentation modulus (E IT) of the nanodiamond enhanced and tungsten strengthened aluminum alloys, which were exposed to the Outer Space environment, was higher by 1.4% than the indentation modulus of the nanodiamod enhanced and tungsten strenghtened aluminum alloy stored under ambient terrestrial conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanical properties of the nanodiamond enhanced and the tungsten strengthened aluminum alloys being exposed in the Outer space.
the influence of the space environment on the microstructure and mechanical properties of the nanodiamond enhanced with tungsten strengthened aluminum.
the mechanical properties of the enhanced with Nanodiamond (ND) and Tungsten (W) strengthened aluminum (Al) alloy (Al-2.8% W-0.5% ND) being exposed to the Outer space environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mechanical characteristics of this nanodiamond enhanced aluminum alloy are not influenced by the exposure to radiation and two-hour cyclic temperature variation in Outer space.
the Outer space environment does not influence the mechanical properties of the investigated nanocomposite material.
the Outer space environment has no influence on the mechanical characteristics (hardness and modulus) of the investigated nanocomposite.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the nanoindentation results show no significant difference between the mechanical characteristics of samples stored in the Outer space and on the Earth, which means no significant effect of the Outer space radiation on the mechanical characteristics.
the mechanical characteristics of both samples are almost the same, and the difference is not more than 2%.
the nanoindentation tests revealed that the Outer space environment did not influence the mechanical properties of the investigated nanomaterial.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Outer space exposure of the nanodiamond enhanced aluminum alloy does not have a significant effect on its mechanical characteristics, as the hardness and modulus values of the sample stored in Outer space are similar to those of the terrestrial sample.
the Outer space environment has not influenced the indentation hardness and indentation modulus of the investigated nanocomposite material.
the mechanical characteristics of nanodiamond enhanced aluminum alloys are not influenced by the Outer space environment.
